source.title_on_document: Establishing the importance of co-creation and self-efficacy in creative collaboration with artificial intelligence

supplement.where: No supplement or online appendix is referred to. Data and syntax files are on the Open Science Framework: https://osf.io/3jqga/ (p. 2, p. 8, p. 9 Data availability).
supplement.holds: Nothing beyond the main text is cited. The OSF repository holds data and SPSS syntax only; all reported statistics are in the main text, Tables 1 and 2, and Figures 3 to 5.

paper_design_summary: Two online experiments on Prolific in which participants wrote an 8-line, two-stanza poem. In Study 1 (96 analyzed) participants were randomly assigned to write alone or to edit a poem produced by the authors' neural poetry generation system (with line alternatives); 50 poems generated by the system alone served as a benchmark. In Study 2 (152 people) a third arm co-wrote the poem with the system, taking turns line by line; poems were rated for creativity by 10 professional poets (Consensual Assessment Technique, 1 to 40 scale), and participants also reported self-rated creativity and (Study 2) creative self-efficacy.

studies.label: Study 1 (poetry writing: human alone vs human-AI editor, plus AI-only poems)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Poetry-writing condition: write a poem unassisted (human condition) or receive a poem generated by the AI poetry system and edit it with the interface tools (human-AI condition). The AI condition consists of 50 poems generated by the system alone, with no participant.
assignment.quote: Participants were randomly allocated to one of two experimental condition groups. ... Condition assignments were random in both studies, with randomization administered via front-end programming.

arms.name: Human condition
arms.description: Wrote an 8-line poem (2 x 4 lines) unassisted, no time limit.

arms.name: Human-AI condition
arms.description: Received a poem produced by the neural poetry generation system and could edit it freely: directly edit any line, choose alternative lines from a dropdown, alternatives update with rhyme constraints; could also delete the poem and start from scratch.

arms.name: AI condition (benchmark, no participants)
arms.description: Poems generated entirely by the poetry generation system, rated alongside participants' poems as a benchmark.

participants.exclusions: 101 recruited via Prolific; six failed an instrumental attention check and were removed from subsequent analyses, leaving 96 (48 per arm). The paper does not say whether the six were excluded before or after random allocation, so no randomized count is recorded.
participants.who: Prolific participants whose first language is English, approval rating at least 97 percent; mean age 27.23 (SD 8.97), 76 percent female; paid GBP2.50.

ai_tool.name_model: Authors' neural poetry generation system (Van de Cruys 2020): recurrent neural encoder-decoder trained on 500 million words of CommonCrawl prose, with an NMF topic model and ABAB rhyme constraints; not an LLM chatbot.
ai_tool.how_used: The system generated a complete 8-line poem from a randomly selected set of three topical words; the participant acted as editor, editing lines directly, choosing alternative candidate lines from a dropdown, or deleting the poem and starting over.

task.description: Write a poem of 8 lines in two stanzas of four lines; rhyme optional.

outcomes.name: Expert evaluations of creativity (CAT), human-AI vs human

outcomes.measure_detail: Consensual Assessment Technique: 10 professional poets (published; 6 with graduate degrees in creative writing, English literature, or related field), each rated all 146 poems (48 human, 48 human-AI, 50 AI) in randomized order, blind to authorship, on a 1 (lowest) to 40 (highest) creativity scale relative to one another. How ratings were aggregated across poets is not stated.

studies.label: Study 2 (poetry writing: human alone vs human-AI editor vs co-creator human-AI)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Poetry-writing condition: unassisted (human), editing a system-generated poem as in Study 1 (human-AI), or co-writing the poem with a redesigned interface in which participant and system alternate lines (co-creator human-AI).
assignment.quote: Participants were randomly allocated to one of three experimental condition groups.

arms.name: Human-AI condition (editor)
arms.description: Same as Study 1: received a complete system-generated poem and edited it with the interface tools.

arms.name: Co-creator human-AI condition
arms.description: Participant chose a set of three topical words, wrote the first line, and the system returned the next line; turns alternated until an 8-line poem; candidate alternative lines available and all lines editable at any stage.

participants.exclusions: None: no participants failed the instrumental attention check.
participants.who: Prolific participants whose first language is English, approval rating at least 97 percent; mean age 35.11 (SD 12.06), 34.9 percent female; paid GBP2.50.
participants.quote: Participants were 152 individuals recruited via Prolific Academic in exchange for GBP2.50 (approximately USD3.00). No participants failed to correctly answer an instrumental attention check.

ai_tool.name_model: Same neural poetry generation system as Study 1 (Van de Cruys 2020), with a redesigned turn-taking interface in the co-creator arm.
ai_tool.how_used: Editor arm: system writes the full poem and the participant edits it. Co-creator arm: participant picks the theme words and writes line 1, the system generates the next line (with candidate alternatives), alternating to 8 lines; the participant can edit any line.

task.description: Write a poem of 8 lines in two stanzas of four lines.
task.duration: Not stated for Study 2 (same procedure as Study 1, which had no time limit).

outcomes.name: Expert evaluations of creativity (CAT)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Consensual Assessment Technique, ratings from 10 different poets (paid USD40 each), 1 to 40 scale as in Study 1. How ratings were aggregated across poets is not stated. Mediation analysis (PROCESS Model 4, 10,000 bootstrap samples) of the condition effect through creative self-efficacy is reported for this outcome.

Table 2: Human-AI 12.53 (4.45), Co-creator 14.70 (5.06), Human 15.74 (4.98). One-way ANOVA F(2, 149) = 5.77, p = 0.004, partial eta2 = 0.07. Figure 4: Delta = 3.21**.

outcomes.name: Self-reported creativity of own poem (not scored on output)
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Self-rating 1 to 40. Listed for completeness; does not meet criterion 3. Creative self-efficacy (Tierney and Farmer 3-item scale, 1 to 7) is also reported: Human-AI 3.74 (1.43), Co-creator 4.62 (1.43), Human 4.71 (1.45); F(2, 149) = 7.01, p = 0.001 (p. 5, Table 2, Figure 3).

contrasts.reported: Human M = 23.29, SD = 9.24 vs human-AI M = 16.96, SD = 9.56; p = 0.001. ANOVA F(2, 149) = 6.08, p = 0.003, eta2 = 0.08. Co-creator M = 21.16, SD = 9.03; higher than human-AI (p = 0.025), not different from human (p = 0.247).

company_involvement.description: Funding from the Ministry of Education, Singapore (11/2019/115); authors declare no competing interests. The AI system is a co-author's academic poetry generator.

eligibility.reason: Both studies randomly allocate individuals to AI-assisted versus unassisted poetry writing (p. 2, p. 4, p. 9). Study 1 analyzes 96 people (48 + 48) and Study 2 analyzes 152 (51/50/51). Creativity of each poem is rated by 10 professional poets (CAT). The AI condition in Study 1 is an AI-vs-human benchmark with no participants and does not count toward the 50. One judgment call: the AI is a recurrent neural poetry generator, not an LLM chatbot; it produces text and line suggestions, which this screener treats as generative AI under the codebook scope.

one_line_finding: Expert-rated poem creativity was lower when participants edited an AI-generated poem than when they wrote alone (Study 1: 12.55 vs 18.23, p < 0.001; Study 2: 12.53 vs 15.74, p = 0.001), while co-writing line by line with the AI (14.70) did not differ from writing alone (p = 0.278) and beat editing (p = 0.026) (p. 4 Table 1; p. 6-7, Table 2).
open_questions: Whether a recurrent encoder-decoder poetry generator (Van de Cruys 2020) counts as generative AI under the codebook scope, which names LLM chatbots and LM-based writing suggestions.

Study 2 text prints the human-condition SD of expert ratings as 9.24 while Table 2 prints 4.98; 9.24 equals the self-reported creativity SD, so the text value is likely a typo, but extraction should use Table 2 and note the discrepancy.
Study 1 ANOVA reports F(2, 145) although 146 poems were rated (which would give df 143); the unit of analysis (poem mean across 10 poets vs individual ratings) is not stated.
Study 1: whether the six attention-check failures were excluded before or after random allocation is not stated; the 48/48 arm counts are after exclusion.
Primary record choice for Study 2: the editor arm (human-AI) versus the co-creator arm against the shared human control. Neither arm is free chatbot use.
notes: No diversity or after-AI outcomes. Pairwise tests are post hoc LSD comparisons after one-way ANOVA; no standard errors for the mean differences are printed, only means, SDs, arm ns, and p-values. Study 2 n per arm for expert ratings is taken from the arm sizes (51/50/51); the paper does not separately report the number of poems rated in Study 2. Study 2 text gives co-creator expert rating as 'M = 14.70, SD = 5.06; p = 0.280' and later 'p = 0.278' versus human; the form records 0.278 from the sentence that states the comparison.
